newsitem.title: MEXICO: FEMSA to keep lid on beer prices this yr.
newsitem.headline: FEMSA to keep lid on beer prices this yr.

text.p: Mexican beverage firm Fomentos Economicos Mexicanos SA (FEMSA) said on Monday it will not raise its beer prices for the rest of the year despite a lag between prices and inflation of about 20-30 percent.
"We raised beer prices at the end of February, beginning of March. We don't plan any new increases this year," said Alfredo Livas, finance director at FEMSA.
Livas said, however, that FEMSA's beer prices were still lagging inflation, which totalled about 77 percent in the past two years.
"Inflation during the past two years has totalled about 77 percent, and we have raised beer prices only 50 percent, so we are still down about 20-30 percent in real terms," he said.
Livas spoke to reporters after the firm's quarterly report. The firm registered net profits of 293.48 million pesos versus 554.88 million pesos during the same period of the year before.
FEMSA's beer sales rose 0.5 percent to 4.70 million hectolitres in the quarter versus the first quarter last year.
Livas said he doubted March's 22 percent rise in beer prices would hurt beer sales volumes during this year, which he said would rise by slightly more than the rate of economic growth.
